**Takeaway:** NVDA is the clear margin leader and fastest grower of the three; AAPL remains the largest by absolute revenue; AMD trails on both profitability metrics but is growing faster than AAPL.

**Trend across periods shown:** Only one fiscal year per company is displayed, so no multi-period trend can be traced. The year-over-year growth rates give a sense of momentum: NVDA grew revenue at [[F4]], AMD at [[F8]], and AAPL at [[F12]]. Note that the fiscal years end up to four months apart—NVDA's FY2026 ended January 2026, AMD's FY2025 ended December 2025, and AAPL's FY2025 ended September 2025—so the periods are not perfectly aligned.

**What is strong and weak:** NVDA's gross margin of [[F2]] and net margin of [[F3]] are the highest of the three, reflecting a far more profitable revenue base than either peer. AMD's net margin of [[F7]] is the lowest, sitting well below AAPL's [[F11]]. On gross margin, AMD's [[F6]] is only slightly above AAPL's [[F10]], but AMD's net margin is less than half of AAPL's, indicating heavier operating costs relative to revenue. NVDA's revenue of [[F1]] is larger than AMD's [[F5]] but smaller than AAPL's [[F9]].

**Counterpoint:** AMD's revenue growth of [[F8]] is healthy and far outpaces AAPL's [[F12]], suggesting AMD is still in a scaling phase. Management attributed a headwind to U.S. export controls on its MI308 data center GPU, which led to approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the quarter ending June 2025 [[C1]]. That charge likely depressed AMD's net margin for the fiscal year shown.

**What the data cannot tell:** No prior-year revenue or margin figures are shown for any of the three companies, so we cannot assess whether margins expanded or contracted. No segment or product-line breakdown is provided, so we cannot see how much of NVDA's margin advantage comes from data-center mix versus other segments. No quarterly progression is shown, so the trajectory within each fiscal year is unknown.

> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** AMD's lower net margin relative to its gross margin could reflect elevated R&D or restructuring costs, given the gap between [[F6]] and [[F7]].
> **Unverified hypothesis (medium confidence):** NVDA's margin premium could reflect pricing power in data-center GPUs, given the combination of [[F2]] and [[F4]].
